newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt up, focus on Brazil, Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt up, focus on Brazil, Mexico.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were higher in afternoon trade, bolstered by news of Brazil's $750 million global bond and Mexico's new economic pact (pacto) between business, government and labor, sources said.

"I think the two things dominating the market right now are the Brazil debt issue and the pacto," said one emerging market debt source. However, he said the market will be especially focused on U.S. economic data due later this week.
Earlier today, Brazil launched a $750 million five-year global bond via J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg at a yield spread of 265 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
"I think it (the Brazil global bond) went reasonably well," said one source.
Sources said stability in the Mexican peso following the renewal of the pacto on Saturday had also helped the broader Latin American emerging debt market.
"Certainly the pacto played a role (in today's rebound)," said the head trader at one investment bank. "It has probably taken some uncertainty out of the market."

At 1530 EST/2030 GMT, Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 7/8 higher at 80-1/2 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 1/4 firmer at 67-7/8 bid and Mexican UMS-26 bonds MXUMS=RR were 7/8 stronger at 97-5/8 bid.
Emerging market debt instruments, which failed to keep pace with U.S. Treasuries Friday, staged a rebound after last week's correction and some sources attributed the bounce to an oversold condition.

"I think what is pushing the market up is the fact that on Friday we had strong rally at the end of the day (in U.S. Treasuries) and a lot of our instruments lagged so now they are catching up," said one source.

"Overall, the market has indeed bounced back. I think the correction was probably somewhat overdone," said another. But he said the market will still probably be somewhat cautious ahead of Friday's U.S. employment report.
Other U.S. data due out includes the third quarter employment cost index on Tuesday and the preliminary third quarter gross domestic product (GDP) on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, sources said continued concern over the health of President Boris Yeltsin and the fact that the INternational Monetary Fund (IMF) withheld a payment from Russia last week still weighed on Russian dollar loans.
Vneshekonombank dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were one percentage point lower at 72-1/4 bid.
ELsewhere, Bulgaria's preliminary election results, showed that the country's ruling ex-communists suffered the worst defeat in their history.
With almost all results counted, opposition candidate Peter Stoyanov, had a clear lead of about 44.9 percent of the vote but was short of a first round victory. A second round will be held on Sunday.
